headline: DRI seizes 76 kg methamphetamine tablets in two operations along North-Eastern frontier
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes 76 kg methamphetamine tablets in two operations along North-Eastern frontier

Contraband was concealed in specially fabricated cavities in automobiles; two persons arrested

28 AUG 2026 12:12AM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on narcotics trafficking along North-Eastern frontier, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in two intelligence-led operations in Assam and Mizoram has seized 76 kg Methamphetamine tablets. Two persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

56 kg seized methamphetamine

On 25.08.26, in the latest intelligence led operation, the officers of DRI, assisted by personnel of 38th Battalion, Assam Rifles, Silchar, intercepted a suspect 12-wheeler truck at Lalpani, around 40 km from Silchar near the Assam-Manipur border. The truck was identified from among a large convoy of vehicles arriving from Jiribam, Manipur.

Thorough examination of the truck led to the detection of a specially fabricated concealed cavity in the driver’s cabin behind the driver’s seat, which contained 36 brick-sized packets weighing 1 kg each and 100 smaller packets weighing 200 grams each, containing pinkish-orange tablets suspected to be Methamphetamine.

Preliminary testing of the samples using the field detection kit indicated the presence of Amphetamine. The recovered contraband, weighing 56 kg along with the truck was seized under the relevant provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985. The occupant of the vehicle was also arrested.

Earlier, on 18.08.2026, in another intelligence-led operation along the Aizawl–Champhai Road in Mizoram, officers of DRI intercepted a car at Bung Bangla, approximately 30 km from Aizawl. Detailed rummaging of the vehicle resulted in the recovery of 64 assorted-sized packets containing 20 kg of pinkish-orange tablets suspected to be methamphetamine, concealed inside specially designed deep cavities in the rocker panels/side sills along both sides of the vehicle and in the space between the fuel tank and the floor of the car.

20 kg seized methamphetamine operation

Tests conducted using the NDPS field test kit indicated the presence of amphetamine. Preliminary investigation indicated that the drugs had been smuggled from Myanmar into Mizoram through the Zokhawthar–Champhai sector. The 20 kg contraband along with the vehicle used for its transportation, was seized under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985. The driver of the vehicle was arrested.

Methamphetamine is a potent synthetic psychostimulant with a high potential for abuse and dependence. Its illicit consumption can cause serious physical and psychological consequences, including cardiovascular complications, agitation, paranoia and psychosis, while prolonged abuse can lead to severe dependence and neurological and behavioural impairment. Methamphetamine is notified as a psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985, and its illicit manufacture, possession, transportation and trafficking attract stringent penal consequences.

27 AUG 2026 9:31PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today attended the PharmaInnova Awards Ceremony-2026, organised by Troika Pharmaceuticals, as the Chief Guest in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has set a goal before the nation that when India celebrates the centenary of its Independence, the country should be number one in the world in every field. India should be secure, educated, develop while preserving its civilisational values, and occupy a leading position among the world’s economies. India has the strength to achieve all this, and we need to channelise this strength, formulate policies accordingly, and take the policy framework down to the grassroots level from an implementation perspective. When Modi Ji became the Prime Minister of the country in 2014, India was the world’s 11th-largest economy, and in just the last 12 years, we have become the world’s fourth-largest economy.

Shri Amit Shah said that the COVID-19 crisis proved that India handled the pandemic in the best possible manner in the world. He said this was because while governments across the world fought the COVID-19 pandemic, in India, the people, State Governments and the Central Government fought it together.

Union Home Minister said that our youth built and launched a private satellite into space at a cost 22 times lower than that in the United States, and today, millions of startups are emerging across the country. During the COVID-19 pandemic, India was among the first three countries in the world to develop a vaccine. We not only vaccinated our own people but also sent vaccines to 70 countries across the world, helping save lives there. What is needed is for India to overcome its inferiority complex, to encourage our youth and instil confidence and enthusiasm in them that we can do it—and we have already demonstrated that we can.

Shri Amit Shah said that in 2014, India was counted among the “Fragile Five” and it was said that the country was suffering from policy paralysis. The same India has today emerged as one of the world’s most attractive manufacturing hubs and has earned global recognition. We have changed the rules, the mindset, the systems and the processes. In 2014, only 1.8 crore households in the country had toilets, whereas today, 13 crore households have toilets. There is a very strong correlation between a person’s health and the availability of a toilet at home, because sanitation plays a major role in preventing diseases. Similarly, today, 16 crore households receive clean drinking water through taps.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that the Modi Government introduced the Ayushman Bharat scheme for the poorest sections of society in India, under which the Government of India bears the entire cost of treatment up to ₹5 lakh. There are 70 crore people in the country for whose treatment expenses coverage was initiated under the scheme. In the healthcare sector, we have adopted a holistic healthcare approach and worked simultaneously on patient care, health infrastructure, medicines, research and development, and manufacturing. Subsequently, ₹1.60 lakh crore was spent on rural health infrastructure, followed by the establishment of a network of hospitals and the expansion of hospital facilities into rural areas. Now, it is the turn of the pharmaceutical industry. India must not only become self-reliant in the field of medicines but also take on the responsibility of supplying medicines to the world.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, the Modi Government has also implemented the PLI scheme in this sector. We have provided incentives for manufacturing critical APIs, Key Starting Materials and medical devices in India. Through the Bulk Drug Park and Medical Device Park policies, a world-class manufacturing ecosystem is being created in India for the entire world. During the COVID-19 pandemic, even under such extremely challenging circumstances, after meeting the requirements of 140 crore people, India became a net exporter of PPE kits and N-95 masks. Within 13 months, we developed both our vaccines, Covaxin and Covishield. These Bulk Drug Parks and the PLI scheme formulated for the pharmaceutical sector are going to prove highly effective in the coming days, both in strengthening India’s pharmaceutical industry and in breaking China’s dominance in this sector. So far, investments worth ₹42,700 crore have been made under these initiatives, and India has exported drugs worth more than ₹3.64 lakh crore.

Union Home Minister said that every company will have to focus on research and encourage students engaged in research, meritorious students and professionals. The Government of India has also introduced three good schemes to promote research. Unless we promote research, we cannot move forward. We have also formulated a national policy to promote research and innovation in the pharma and medtech sectors. The PRIP scheme is a multi-thousand-crore-rupee initiative through which the government can support you. Shri Shah said that today we are also manufacturing ventilators, and an ecosystem is being created under which all medical devices will begin to be manufactured in India before 2028.

headline: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Summer Moong Procurement and Crop Insurance Implementation in Madhya Pradesh
fullText:

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Summer Moong Procurement and Crop Insurance Implementation in Madhya Pradesh

Record Summer Moong Procurement in MP: 5.33 Lakh Tonnes Procured, Farmers Gain from MSP Support

NAFED, NCCF Drive Summer Moong Procurement in MP, Delivering Direct Benefits to Farmers: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

27 AUG 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today held a virtual review meeting with the Agriculture and Horticulture Ministers of Madhya Pradesh at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The meeting reviewed the procurement of summer Moong in Madhya Pradesh, the benefits of Minimum Support Price for farmers, and issues related to the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. During the meeting, Shri Chouhan said that, at the request of the Madhya Pradesh government, the Government of India had initially approved the procurement of 4,54,580 metric tonnes of summer Moong for the 2026 season. Subsequently, keeping farmers' interests in mind, an additional 84,492 metric tonnes was approved. The additional approval did not impose any financial burden on the state government.

With this, the total approved procurement quantity of summer Moong for Madhya Pradesh in the 2026 season stood at 5,39,072 metric tonnes. The procurement period has now ended, with the state recording procurement of 5.33 lakh metric tonnes of Moong. The procurement remained within the approved limit, and all willing and registered farmers were able to sell their available produce. The procurement enabled farmers to receive a fair price for their produce at MSP, providing them direct financial benefit

Procurement operations were carried out mainly through NAFED and NCCF, with particular emphasis on timely payments to farmers and maintaining transparency throughout the process. The procurement also contributed to strengthening the rural economy. Madhya Pradesh also recorded improved performance in Moong procurement compared to the previous year. During summer 2025, against an approved quantity of 4,19,692 metric tonnes, the state had procured 3,93,123.79 metric tonnes. In summer 2026, both the approved quantity and actual procurement increased. Shri Chouhan said the improvement reflected greater support for farmers and increased confidence in the market.

Review of Crop Insurance Implementation

The meeting also reviewed the implementation of the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) in Madhya Pradesh under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. The state government had requested the finalisation of the term sheet for implementing the scheme. Shri Chouhan said the Central Government had taken the necessary steps in this regard, provided the term sheet to the state government, and urged its early implementation.

The meeting also reviewed progress on the implementation of the WINDS system in Madhya Pradesh. The concerned Central department has written to the state government from time to time regarding implementation of the system, but its rollout in the state is still pending. Officials noted that effective implementation of RWBCIS would be difficult without WINDS and stressed the need to operationalise the system at the earliest.

The meeting also discussed the use of technology-based yield assessment under PMFBY. Madhya Pradesh is currently using technology-based yield assessment for major crops. The Central Government suggested reintroducing Crop Cutting Experiments to enable ground-truthing and recalibration of technology-based models.

A blended approach, combining technology-based assessments with field-level data, was also recommended to improve coordination and enhance the reliability of yield assessment. Shri Chouhan said the Central and state governments would work together to further strengthen procurement, payment and crop insurance systems in the interest of farmers. He said that timely procurement, assured MSP and an effective crop insurance system are essential to strengthening farmers' incomes and their confidence in the agricultural market.

headline: Union Health Minister Reviews Progress of Key Health Sector Projects Announced in Union Budget 2026-27
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Reviews Progress of Key Health Sector Projects Announced in Union Budget 2026-27

160 District Hospitals to be Strengthened in First Phase by March 2027; Focus on Expanding Emergency and Trauma Care Capacity

Review focuses on strengthening drug regulation, expanding allied healthcare workforce, enhancing mental health and trauma care, and developing medical value tourism infrastructure

27 AUG 2026 9:03PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today reviewed the progress of key projects and initiatives announced for the health sector in the Union Budget 2026-27, with a focus on ensuring their timely implementation, effective inter-ministerial coordination and delivery of measurable outcomes. During the review, Shri Nadda took stock of the preparatory work undertaken by various departments of the Ministry and emphasised that Budget announcements should translate into concrete programmes, strengthened institutions and enhanced healthcare capacities within clearly defined timelines.

The Minister reviewed the progress of the initiative to increase emergency and trauma care capacity in District Hospitals by 50 per cent through establishment and strengthening of Emergency and Trauma Care Centres. He was informed that, following a post-Budget webinar, three committees were constituted to examine infrastructure, drugs, diagnostics and quality; human resources, academic expansion and skilling; and digital architecture and pre-hospital integration. A comprehensive gap analysis of District Hospitals against the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) has also been completed. Based on patient load, infrastructure and overall readiness, 613 District Hospitals have been categorised for phased implementation, with 160 District Hospitals identified for Phase I and targeted for strengthening by March 2027. Phase II will cover 203 District Hospitals and Phase III the remaining 250. Shri Nadda stressed the need for close monitoring so that the first phase progresses in a focused and time-bound manner.

The Minister also reviewed the progress of National Emergency Life Support (NELS) training, aimed at strengthening the emergency care skills and competencies of healthcare professionals and frontline personnel. The training is envisaged to enhance preparedness for timely assessment, stabilisation and management of patients with life-threatening conditions, thereby complementing the expansion of emergency and trauma care capacity in District Hospitals.

The Minister also reviewed progress on the Budget initiative to strengthen the Allied Health Professionals (AHPs) ecosystem, with the objective of adding 1 lakh AHPs over the next five years across 10 selected disciplines. He was informed that consultations have been undertaken with industry, State Governments, Central and State Government institutions and hospitals, implementing agencies and regulatory bodies. A draft Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) note has been prepared and circulated to concerned Ministries and NITI Aayog. The Minister was further apprised of the meeting held under the chairpersonship of the Hon’ble Finance Minister on 27 July 2026, with discussions continuing on funding options, including a feasible Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.

The Minister took a detailed review of the initiatives being progressed by the Department of Health Research, including Biopharma SHAKTI and the establishment of five Regional Medical Hubs. Under Biopharma SHAKTI, consultations with industry stakeholders, sensitisation meetings with medical colleges and clinical-trial training workshops have been undertaken towards creating a network of more than 1,000 accredited clinical trial sites. The proposed ₹500-crore initiative envisages a hub-and-spoke trial-site network, strengthened data and digital systems, a central trial facilitation agency and a site accreditation framework. Shri Nadda reviewed the progress and stressed the importance of building the requisite institutional and research ecosystem to support India’s biopharmaceutical and clinical research capabilities.

Reviewing the proposal for five Regional Medical Hubs, the Minister was informed that inputs have been shared with DPIIT and five priority disease areas—dyslipidaemia, generalized anxiety disorder, cardiovascular diseases, insomnia and osteoarthritis—have been identified for development of evidence-based integrative treatment protocols. ICMR and CCRAS nodal persons have also been identified for the proposed working groups. Shri Nadda emphasised the importance of coordinated efforts across relevant institutions to ensure that the initiative contributes meaningfully to India’s emerging medical value tourism ecosystem.

The Minister also reviewed the progress of the Budget proposal to strengthen the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to meet global standards and approval timeframes through a dedicated scientific review cadre and specialist workforce. He was informed that the Expert Committee constituted to finalise the workforce structure, number of positions, pay levels and the permanent and flexible mix at different levels has submitted its report. Shri Nadda stressed the need to further strengthen regulatory capacity and scientific expertise to support an efficient, robust and globally benchmarked drug regulatory system.

The progress of initiatives for strengthening mental healthcare was also reviewed, including the establishment of NIMHANS-II and upgradation of the Central Institute of Psychiatry (CIP), Ranchi and Lokopriya Gopinath Bordoloi Regional Institute of Mental Health (LGBRIMH), Tezpur as Regional Apex Institutions. The Minister was informed that the Expert Committee on NIMHANS-II has submitted its report and that the proposed institute is envisaged with a capacity of 1,000 beds. The proposed strengthening of CIP, Ranchi and LGBRIMH, Tezpur includes advanced psychiatry, neurology and neurosurgery facilities, along with enhanced research, training and academic capacities. As an immediate institutional support measure, NIMHANS, Bengaluru will mentor both institutions to address identified gaps relating to administrative and institutional frameworks, academic flexibility, research development, clinical administration and community integration.

Shri Nadda further reviewed the proposal to support States in establishing five Regional Medical Hubs in partnership with the private sector to promote India as a global destination for medical value tourism. The proposed hubs are envisaged to integrate medical, educational and research facilities with AYUSH Centres, Medical Value Tourism Facilitation Centres, diagnostics, post-care and rehabilitation infrastructure. The Minister was apprised of consultations held with NATHEALTH, FICCI, Services Export Promotion Council, Invest India, NABH and QCI, as well as capacity-building workshops, including a regional workshop in Hyderabad. Actionable points emerging from these consultations will be forwarded to the National Medical and Wellness Tourism Promotion Board (NMWTPB), Ministry of Tourism, for appropriate action.

During the review, Shri Nadda underscored that the various Budget initiatives are closely interconnected and require sustained coordination between departments, Ministries, States, institutions and other stakeholders. He emphasised time-bound implementation, regular monitoring and inter-ministerial coordination, with particular attention to clearly defined deliverables and measurable outcomes. He also stressed that preparatory work, including expert consultations, institutional assessments, gap analysis and development of implementation frameworks, should be translated into visible progress on the ground.

The initiatives reviewed by the Minister collectively seek to strengthen emergency and trauma care, allied healthcare and caregiving workforce, drug regulatory capacity, clinical research and biopharmaceutical capabilities, mental healthcare, medical education and specialised healthcare infrastructure. The first phase of strengthening 160 District Hospitals by March 2027, along with the ongoing training and planned skilling of 1.5 lakh caregivers, reflects the Government’s emphasis on converting Budget announcements into tangible improvements in healthcare delivery and workforce capacity.

The meeting was attended by Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava; Secretary, Department of Health Research, Dr. Rajiv Bahl; Additional Secretary and MD (NHM), Smt. Aradhana Patnaik; Additional Secretary (Medical Education), Smt. Vinod Kotwal; Additional Secretary, Shri Vijay Nehra; and all Joint Secretaries and other senior officers of the Ministry.

Union Home Minister and Minister of CooperationShri Amit Shah today addressed the 72nd convocation of Gujarat Vidyapith in Ahmedabad as the chief guest. Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Addressing the convocation, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that today 900 students of Gujarat Vidyapith are receiving their degrees and entering social life, and that this is a precious moment inthe lives of these students.

Shri Amit Shah said that he has been an admirer of Mahatma Gandhi since childhood. His mother too has been a devoted follower of Mahatma Gandhi. Shri Shah said that in the early years of his life he wove khadi and also spun yarn. He said that his mother took a vow from him to wear khadi throughout his life.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Gujarat Vidyapith is the very place where strategy used to be formulated to win the country its freedom in the independence struggle, and where great men such as Acharya J. B. Kripalani and Kaka Saheb Kalelkar worked to awaken the people for Indianness and the mother tongue. He said that when Mahatma Gandhi laid the foundation of Gujarat Vidyapith, he had decided that after India became free, Gujarat Vidyapith itself would create the model for the Indian education system.

Shri Amit Shah appealed to the students receiving their degrees from Gujarat Vidyapith today to be sure to set the goal of their lives before leaving the campus. While setting that goal, there should be no burden in the mind about whether the goal will be achieved or not. He said one should never think whether the work can be done or not, but whether the work is worth doing.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah told the students that one should never set goals for oneself, but rather set them for the nation, society, the people, and especially the poor. If a goal is set for society and the nation, the burden of victory or defeat will not remain on you. No matter how many difficulties one faces in life, there will never be any room for disappointment. If goals are set for oneself and one’s family, difficulties can lead to disappointment, and one may even lose one’s way. Citing his own example, Shri Shah said that he had faced many difficulties in life, but he never became disappointed. He said the reason was that the goals he had set were neither for himself nor for his family. That is why his enthusiasm to work always remained intact. He said that despite all efforts to discourage him, he was never disheartened.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that he has read about, understood and imbibed the thoughts of many great personalities in his life. However, the message of Mahatma Gandhi was relevant then, is relevant today, and will remain relevant for the next 100 years. He said that Gandhi Ji’s message shows the path of welfare to the entire world. Indian ways of life, Indian values and traditions are the fundamental basis of Gandhi Ji’s message, and therefore, it will never become irrelevant.

Shri Amit Shah said that today, 900 students are graduating from Gujarat Vidyapith with degrees and 11 gold medals. Going forward, they will have to face many family and social challenges, but these can be overcome through daily practice and self-study. He said that Gujarat Vidyapith is based on Mahatma Gandhi’s concept of Basic Education, which emphasises village-centric development and the transition from “self” to “others”—that is, an education that teaches us to think of everyone rather than just ourselves. He said that after returning to India, Mahatma Gandhi, following the advice of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, travelled across the country. Despite the immense diversity of languages, dialects, attire, food habits and religions, when he returned, he told Dr. Rajendra Prasad in Champaran that he had witnessed a remarkable sense of unity in the country. He worked to translate this unity into reality through numerous experiments, and Gujarat Vidyapith became a laboratory for these efforts. Shri Shah said that, in accordance with Gandhi Ji’s thoughts and guidance, Gujarat Vidyapith was established on October 18, 1920.

Shri Amit Shah said that Mahatma Gandhi believed that independence remains incomplete until our language, culture, labour and objectives are aligned with the national interest. He believed that Swaraj can never be achieved without one’s own language. He said that if we are not connected with our religion and culture, freedom has no meaning. If our labour and our objectives are not connected with our nation, then even after attaining independence, we will not be able to protect it.

The Home Minister said that the objective of education should be to rebuild the nation through the harmonious integration of the hands, the heart and the mind. Education should impart skills to the hands, awaken sensitivity in the heart, and equip the mind with knowledge along with wisdom and discernment. He said that a mind filled with knowledge alone can give rise to arrogance, whereas a mind enriched with knowledge and wisdom fosters humility and scholarship.

Shri Amit Shah said that the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 rests on five pillars—mother tongue, skills, multidisciplinary learning, the Indian knowledge tradition, and holistic personality development. In a way, this is the same education system that India had imparted to the world for centuries, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji has now brought that very education system back for the youth of India. He said that without changing its core essence, modern advancements from across the world have been incorporated into the National Education Policy.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Mahatma Gandhi identified seven social sins. If these seven social sins are avoided, 90% of the evils in society can be eliminated. These include politics without principles, business without morality, wealth without labour, pleasure without conscience, knowledge without character, science without humanity, and worship without sacrifice. He said that all young people should always remember these seven social sins. He added that none of us is a great personality who can claim that we would never commit any of these sins. However, if we remain conscious of them, we will hesitate and stop ourselves when faced with the temptation to commit them; and if we ever do commit one, we will also be willing to repent and atone for it.

Shri Amit Shah said that Mahatma Gandhi had prescribed 11 vows, including non-violence, non-stealing, celibacy, non-possession, physical labour, control of the palate, fearlessness, equal respect for all religions, Swadeshi, and the removal of un-touchability. These 11 vows remain relevant even today, and we should move forward by following them. He said that Gandhi Ji had described religious conversion as a sin. The students have also taken a pledge today to live according to their own ‘Swadharma’.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Khadi is not merely a fabric or an economic activity; it is an idea that one should uphold the spirit of Swadeshi in every aspect of one’s life. He said that the turnover of Khadi and Village Industries was ₹31,000 crore in 2013–14, which increased to ₹1.87 lakh crore in 2025–26. He said that Mahatma Gandhi placed great emphasis on cleanliness, and today there is not a single household in the country without a toilet. He added that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has worked to instil the values of cleanliness in the new generation by integrating them with education.

Shri Amit Shah said that there is no objection to learning any language in the world when it comes to knowledge of languages. However, there can be no greater mistake than thinking that speaking in one’s own language will make one inferior. Language is what connects us with the values, history and roots of our country. That is why Gandhi Ji also emphasised the importance of one’s own language. He said that Gandhi Ji also placed emphasis on Gram Swaraj, Gram Samriddhi and cooperation. The Modi Government is working afresh in all three of these areas.

The Home Minister said that even during the period of colonial rule, despite facing repeated setbacks, Gandhi Ji always used the term ‘Punar – Nirman’ of the nation, rather than ‘Navnirman’. Gandhi Ji believed that the principles that had been followed for thousands of years would remain unchanged; however, we would modernise and undertake reconstruction. Shri Shah said that over the past 12 years, the country has embarked on the path of reconstruction. The Modi Government has made a concerted effort from 2014 to 2026 to move forward with the nation’s strength, prosperity, security, self-reliance, and ethics in leadership as its core principles. He said that when the country completed 75 years of Independence, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi placed a resolve before the youth of the country that by 2047, the centenary year of India’s Independence, India should be number one in the world in every field. He said that if we become number one, we will not think only about ourselves but about the welfare of the entire universe. We will be powerful, but our power will be used with wisdom and discretion. We will be prosperous, but that prosperity will be for every citizen of the country and for every suffering person across the world. It is with this vision that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has presented the vision of India in 2047 before today’s youth.

headline: "Students of Today Are the Torchbearers of Democracy Tomorrow": CEC Gyanesh Kumar
fullText:
Election Commission

"Students of Today Are the Torchbearers of Democracy Tomorrow": CEC Gyanesh Kumar

27 AUG 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Election Commission of India (ECI) organised its third regional conference on "Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELC 2.0) and ECINET" in Chennai today, focusing on strengthening electoral literacy and democratic awareness among young citizens. Addressing the gathering, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar said that the students of today are the torchbearers of democracy tomorrow. He added that Electoral Literacy Clubs (ELCs) across India will help strengthen the backbone of the world's oldest and largest democracy.

Addressing the participants comprising students and teachers from schools, colleges and universities across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar described students as the future of the nation and emphasised that engaging young citizens and securing their trust and informed participation in the electoral process is an investment in the future of democracy.

CEC Shri Gyanesh Kumar stated how elections in India are held strictly as per the Constitution of India, law and instructions issued by ECI and are conducted transparently under the concurrent audit of political parties, candidates or their representatives at all stages. He underlined the need for students and young electors to familiarise themselves with India’s electoral system, democratic values, electoral registration, polling and counting processes, and the role and functioning of the Election Commission of India.

ELC 2.0, with the tagline "Learn Democracy. Lead Democracy.", reimagines Electoral Literacy Clubs as structured, visible and digitally enabled platforms across schools, colleges and universities, encouraging young and first-time voters to understand and meaningfully participate in democracy. Leveraging the extensive ECINet digital platform, which provides all election-related services from roll to poll, the initiative will drive continuous, year-round electoral literacy activities through a dedicated ELC portal, building a streamlined pan-India network of ELCs.

The initiative assumes significance in view of India’s extensive educational ecosystem, comprising approximately 15 lakh schools with nearly 25 crore students and over one crore teachers. The higher education sector comprises nearly 1,500 universities and around 70,000 educational institutions, with an estimated enrolment of 4.33 crore students.

Through this extensive institutional network, ELC 2.0 seeks to promote factual and experiential electoral education, enhance awareness of India’s electoral system, and encourage young citizens to become ambassadors of informed democratic participation. The ELCs will also disseminate information on electoral registration, polling, counting, ECINet App and other key ECI initiatives.

Earlier in the day, in an interactive session with over 500 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) of Tamil Nadu, CEC Gyanesh Kumar congratulated the BLOs for their service which resulted in smooth execution of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls in the State. He also congratulated them for the highest-ever poll-participation in the recently concluded Legislative Assembly elections in the State with 4.93 crore votes polled and 86.03% voter turnout which was the highest ever in the history of the State.

The students and the BLOs had a Question-and-Answer session with the CEC as part of the meeting. BLOs had an opportunity to clarify their doubts directly through the interaction.

headline: Student’s Suggestion Prompts Sarbananda Sonowal to Announce Swimming Pool at Dibrugarh University

Top-performing university athletes to be sent for National Sports Excursion

We Must Take India’s Sporting Culture Deeper Into Educational Institutions: Sarbananda Sonowal

Sonowal interacted with Dibrugarh University Students at PM Narendra Modi ‘Khelo India Samvaad

PM Modi Addresses Nearly 8 Lakh Youth, Calls for Sports to Drive a Healthy, Strong & Self-Reliant India

27 AUG 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

A student’s suggestion during an interaction with Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal at Dibrugarh University in Dibrugarh, Assam, at the ‘Khelo India Dialogue’ has led to the announcement of a swimming pool on the university campus. Sonowal also announced a national sports excursion for the university’s top-performing athletes.

During the interaction, a student raised the need for swimming facilities at the university and asked whether students could be taught swimming, particularly because Dibrugarh and surrounding areas are prone to flooding. Taking note of the suggestion, Sonowal announced that immediate initiative will be taken to develop a swimming pool within the university campus.

The student’s intervention brought a practical dimension to the dialogue, highlighting how sports infrastructure can also address local needs. Besides promoting swimming as a competitive sport, the proposed facility would provide students an opportunity to acquire important water-safety and life skills in a flood-prone region.

“The suggestion raised by the student today reflects the kind of practical thinking and awareness we want to encourage among our young people. In a flood-prone region like Dibrugarh and other adjoining areas, learning to swim is not only about pursuing a sport but also about developing an essential life skill. The proposed swimming pool will create an opportunity for students to learn, train and pursue swimming in a structured environment,” Sonowal said.

Sonowal also joined the students in listening to an address by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the country’s youth. He interacted with the students on the role of sports and fitness in building a healthy and resilient society.

Indian football legend and former national team captain Baichung Bhutia was also present at the programme and addressed the students. His remarks and interaction with the students added to the sporting focus of the event.

Speaking on the occasion, Sonowal said the enthusiasm displayed by students toward sports was encouraging. He said sports are an important means of building healthy individuals and a healthy society and should become an integral part of the lives of young people.

“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has given unprecedented importance to sports, fitness and the development of young sporting talent through initiatives such as Khelo India and Fit India. Our focus is to take this sporting culture deeper into educational institutions, provide young athletes with better infrastructure and exposure, and create opportunities for the youth of Assam and the Northeast to compete and excel at the national and international levels,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

Sarbananda Sonowal highlighted Prime Minister Modi’s ‘Fit India’ vision and his call to make sports an integral part of everyday life. He said the focus on sports was not limited to developing international-level athletes but also aimed at encouraging young people to lead healthier lives and contribute to building a stronger and self-reliant India.

Sonowal further announced that Dibrugarh University’s top-performing athletes will undertake a national sports excursion. The exposure visit will give promising athletes an opportunity to experience a premier national sports training ecosystem and gain insights into high-performance training and sporting practices.

The programme saw enthusiastic participation from students, who interacted with the speakers and shared their views and suggestions on sports and fitness. Sonowal said the combination of student-led suggestions, better sporting infrastructure and exposure to national-level training facilities can help strengthen the sporting ecosystem and create greater opportunities for young athletes from Assam and the Northeast.

headline: From Daily-Wage Work to Scientist-C: How NFSC Support Enabled Tamil Nadu Scholar Karnan A to Build a Distinguished Research Career
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Daily-Wage Work to Scientist-C: How NFSC Support Enabled Tamil Nadu Scholar Karnan A to Build a Distinguished Research Career

27 AUG 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance at the right stage can enable talented scholars from disadvantaged backgrounds to continue higher education, pursue meaningful research and build careers that contribute to national development.

Karnan A, a 30-year-old scholar from Sivagangai district in Tamil Nadu, experienced this transformation through support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme. He is now a full-time employee serving as Scientist-C at the CSIR Fourth Paradigm Institute, Bengaluru.

Karnan belongs to a Scheduled Caste community and is the first researcher in his family and among the very few researchers from his community. His parents are seasonal farmers with limited and irregular income, while his two brothers also depended on the same family income for their education.

From school through postgraduate studies, Karnan undertook daily-wage work on weekends to pay his fees and meet basic needs. During the final year of his postgraduate course, he began taking tuition classes, but the income remained insufficient. In 2017, he cleared the National Eligibility Test for Lectureship on his first attempt but narrowly missed the Junior Research Fellowship cut-off.

Without a fellowship, Karnan had to meet his PhD fees and research expenses entirely through income from tuition classes. He also lacked academic guidance, mentorship and professional networks as the first researcher from his village and one of the very few in his taluk. These economic, educational and social barriers made it extremely difficult for him to continue his doctoral studies without burdening his family.

A turning point came in 2019 when Karnan was selected for the NFSC fellowship based on his December 2018 CSIR-UGC NET Lectureship score. His assistance commenced in September 2019, and he received approximately Rs 16 lakh in the form of fellowship support, House Rent Allowance and contingency assistance.

The fellowship gave Karnan financial freedom for the first time in his academic life. He no longer had to depend on daily-wage work or tuition income to meet his fees and research expenses. The resulting confidence and peace of mind enabled him to focus fully on his research. Motivated by the support, he appeared for the NET examination again and successfully qualified for the Junior Research Fellowship.

Karnan completed his PhD, and his thesis received a 'Highly Commended' distinction. He published six research articles in SCI/SCIE-indexed international journals. After completing his doctorate, he was selected as an Institution of Eminence Postdoctoral Fellow at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, with a fellowship of Rs 67,000 per month along with HRA.

headline: From Sanitation Worker to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneur: NAMASTE-SUY Enables Himanshu to Build a Safer and Dignified Livelihood
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Sanitation Worker to Mechanised Sanitation Entrepreneur: NAMASTE-SUY Enables Himanshu to Build a Safer and Dignified Livelihood

27 AUG 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

Timely financial assistance and access to mechanised equipment can enable sanitation workers to move away from unsafe work, become self-employed and build secure livelihoods with dignity.

Himanshu, a 25-year-old graduate from the OBC Lohar community, experienced this transformation through assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE Scheme. A resident of Village Nandgram, Mariyam Nagar, Ghaziabad, he now independently operates a tractor-cum-suction machine and provides mechanised sanitation services in nearby areas.

Himanshu grew up in a family where financial hardship was part of everyday life. His father worked as a daily-wage labourer, and the family often struggled to meet basic needs. As the eldest son, Himanshu assumed responsibility for supporting his parents and younger siblings at an early age. Difficult financial circumstances compelled him to begin working while pursuing his aspirations for a more secure future.

He entered sanitation-related work under local contractors, undertaking sewer and septic tank cleaning in harsh and risky conditions. The work involved physical exhaustion, irregular wages and dependence on contractors. Social stigma associated with the occupation further affected his confidence and dignity, while the absence of financial assets prevented him from starting independent work.

Despite these challenges, Himanshu remained determined to become self-employed and operate modern sanitation equipment instead of continuing unsafe manual labour. He wanted financial stability and social respect for himself, as well as a secure future for his family. He believed that sanitation workers, when provided appropriate support and opportunities, could become independent entrepreneurs.

A major turning point came when Himanshu received financial assistance under NAMASTE-SUY for procuring a tractor-cum-suction machine. The assistance, released in August 2025, supported a total project cost of Rs 10,70,400, comprising a loan of Rs 6,74,200 and an upfront capital subsidy of Rs 3,96,200.

The tractor-cum-suction machine enabled Himanshu to begin mechanised sanitation service work independently. Mechanisation reduced his dependence on unsafe manual practices and contractors while improving the safety, efficiency and reliability of his operations. Gradually, his work expanded and he came to be recognised not merely as a labourer, but as a young entrepreneur providing dignified sanitation services.

Before receiving support, Himanshu worked as a sanitation labourer and earned an irregular income that was insufficient to meet his family's needs. After establishing his mechanised sanitation service, his financial condition improved significantly. Even after meeting operational expenses and paying a monthly EMI of Rs 15,059, he now earns and saves approximately Rs 25,000-Rs 35,000 per month. His earnings increase further during the rainy and winter seasons because of higher demand for sanitation services.

The improved income has enabled the family to manage household expenses more comfortably and plan for the future with greater confidence. For Himanshu, the most meaningful change is the happiness and relief visible on his parents' faces. Ownership of the sanitation vehicle has also strengthened his confidence, self-respect and sense of independence.

At present, Himanshu successfully operates his tractor-cum-suction machine in nearby areas and continues to expand his sanitation service work. The initiative has provided him with a stable and sustainable income, safer working conditions through mechanisation, improved social dignity and long-term self-employment opportunities.

Standing beside his tractor-cum-suction machine, Himanshu represents the impact of the NAMASTE-SUY Initiative in empowering sanitation workers through mechanisation, financial support and dignified livelihood opportunities. His journey demonstrates how timely assistance, combined with courage and perseverance, can transform years of struggle into self-reliance and inspire others in the community.

Convergence for Rural Development: DDWS urges States/UTs to integrate works of JJM 2.0 and SBM-G 2.0 under VB-G RAM G Act

27 AUG 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, in collaboration with the Ministry of Rural Development, has called for the convergence of works of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) SBM-(G) 2.0 under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025. This convergence is an initiative towards strengthening rural development, integrated planning for rural water security and resilience.

The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 identifies water security as one of its four thematic focus areas, recognising its importance for sustainable livelihoods, agricultural productivity, climate resilience and long-term rural development. The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0, approved on 10 March 2026, places drinking water source sustainability, groundwater recharge and greywater management at the core of its strategy to ensure reliable and resilient rural drinking water services. Similarly, SBM(G) 2.0 focuses on scientific management of solid and liquid waste to improve environmental sanitation and public health. The complementary objectives of these programmes provide an opportunity for integrated planning and implementation through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs).

Under the convergence plan, the States and UTs have been requested to

Ensure proper integrated planning

Prioritise water security under the VGPPs

Include the official in charge of Rural Water Supply/ Public Health Engineering Department in the State-level Steering Committee constituted under the Act

Nominate dedicated nodal officers from State Water and Sanitation Mission and Rural Development Department, with corresponding nodal officers to facilitate planning, implementation and monitoring of convergent activities.

Technically align VGPPs with Village Action Plans under JJM 2.0 and SBM-G 2.0

Register and geo-tag all works under JJM 2.0 and SBM- G 2.0 and other convergent assets on the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack

States to utilise geospatial planning tools such as Yuktdhara, along with water budgeting and hydrogeological assessments

Institutionalise convergence to ensure that investments under VB-G RAM G, JJM 2.0, SBM-G 2.0 collectively contribute to sustainable drinking water security and improved rural livelihoods.

This close coordination among the Departments of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and other concerned departments at the State, district and Gram Panchayat levels is critical for successful implementation. Also, such convergence strengthens the sustainability of rural drinking water services while promoting ecological sustainability, climate resilience and quality of life in rural communities, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

headline: High-Level African Delegation and UNDP Engage with Department of Land Resources on India’s Digital Public Infrastructure in Land Governance
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

High-Level African Delegation and UNDP Engage with Department of Land Resources on India’s Digital Public Infrastructure in Land Governance

Secretary, DoLR highlights the vision of ‘Bharat Land Stack’ and ‘Bhu-Aadhaar’ as transformative DPI tools to unlock economic potential and empower citizens

Technical deep dive showcases DILRMP milestones: Over 40.58 Crore land parcels assigned Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) and near-universal computerisation of land records

Delegates from the African Union, Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and Zambia explore technology adoption, drone-based surveying, and urban land mapping under NAKSHA

27 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level delegation representing the African Union Commission, senior government officials from six African nations (Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and Zambia), and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) visited the Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Government of India, at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi, for an intensive technical engagement on Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) in land governance.

The exposure visit aimed to study India’s pioneering digital transformation in land administration, specifically focusing on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), the Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar), the National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS), and the NAKSHA initiative for urban habitations.

Land Records as Foundational DPI: Unlocking Economic Value

Welcoming the international delegation, the Secretary, Shri Narendra Bhooshan Department of Land Resources, outlined India’s evolutionary trajectory from colonial and legacy land administration systems to a modern, technology-driven, and citizen-centric digital ecosystem. Emphasizing that digital identity served as India’s foundational layer of DPI through Aadhaar, he noted that geospatial land identity—through the 14-digit Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN)—is serving as the next transformative leap.

Addressing the delegates, the Secretary highlighted:

"Land is the largest and most foundational asset class in any developing economy. In traditional systems, without clear spatial titles and interoperability, vast amounts of land remain 'dead capital' that citizens cannot leverage. Our vision under DILRMP and the Bharat Land Stack is to build an unshakeable digital trust architecture. By linking georeferenced land records, circle rates, registration, and encumbrances into a single interoperable layer, we are creating an ecosystem where even the most vulnerable citizen or rural landowner can unlock formal credit and mortgages seamlessly. This experience and architecture are open to be shared with our partner nations across Africa to accelerate DPI-led inclusive growth across the Global South."

Technical Deep Dive: DILRMP and the Multi-Layered Bharat Land Stack

During the technical sessions, Shri Amit Kumar Singh, Director (LR), DoLR, presented a comprehensive overview of the macro reforms and technological framework powering DILRMP.

Key milestones shared with the international delegates included:

99.90% of textual Records of Rights (RoRs) computerised across the country.

97.43% of cadastral maps digitized, with 76.16% of land parcels fully georeferenced.

85.24% spatial-textual integration achieved between cadastral maps and Records of Rights.

Over 40.58 Crore land parcels assigned the 14-digit alphanumeric Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN).

98.96% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) computerised, with 17 States/UTs adopting the centralized NGDRS platform and 17 States operating state-specific digital registration software.

94.11% of Revenue Courts computerised under the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS), enabling real-time litigation marking on property records.

The delegation was given a walkthrough of the Bharat Land Stack—an integrated, GIS-based federated architecture that layers satellite/drone imagery, georeferenced cadastral boundaries, RoRs, property registration data, master planning/zoning regulations, building approvals, restrictions/litigations, circle rates, and tenancy details to provide a single, authoritative digital source of truth.

Next-Generation Urban Mapping: The NAKSHA Programme

Presenting the urban land records initiative, Shri Shyam Kumar, Director (LR) DoLR, briefed the delegation on the NAKSHA (National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations) pilot programme.

The presentation detailed the end-to-end workflow utilizing high-precision surveying technologies:

Deployment of 2D Nadir cameras, 5-camera Oblique systems, and LiDAR sensors mounted on aerial drones to achieve centimetre-level positional accuracy.

Generation of Ortho-Rectified Imagery (ORI), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and 3D Reality Models for complex urban landscapes.

Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GNSS rover-based ground truthing, participatory ground validation, and transparent claims/objections redressal.

Milestone progress in the pilot phase, with aerial flying completed across 145 out of 150 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), leading to the issuance of legally authentic Urban Property (UrPro) Cards.

Fostering South-South Cooperation

The delegation commended India’s scale, technical rigor, and open-architecture approach to digital governance.

During the discussions, representatives from the UNDP emphasized that India’s DPI model offers invaluable blueprints for African economies seeking structural transformation, tenure security, and efficient digital public service delivery.

Officials representing the African Union Commission highlighted the relevance of India's geospatial integration for Africa’s broader digital transformation strategies and data governance frameworks.

Furthermore, senior delegates from the participating partner nations—including Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, and Zambia—engaged in interactive technical discussions on institutional adaptation, legal harmonization, data privacy, and the deployment of drone-based surveys for land mapping.

The visiting UN and UNDP teams appreciated the Department of Land Resources' collaborative approach to sharing knowledge with the global community.

The meeting concluded with a mutual commitment to deepen technical knowledge exchanges, capacity-building partnerships, and South-South collaboration to advance inclusive, transparent, and resilient land governance frameworks globally.

headline: From Financial Challenges to an Academic Career: How NFSC Support Empowered Dr Janaki Sundararajan
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Challenges to an Academic Career: How NFSC Support Empowered Dr Janaki Sundararajan

28 AUG 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi

For full-time research scholars from modest families, meeting the cost of advanced education can be difficult. Timely fellowship assistance can reduce this burden and allow scholars to pursue their academic ambitions with greater confidence and focus.

Demonstrating the impact of support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Dr Janaki Sundararajan, a 32-year-old scholar from Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, overcame financial and academic barriers to complete her Ph.D. and build a career in teaching and research.

Before receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme, Dr Janaki faced financial difficulties in managing research expenses and academic activities during her Ph.D. period from 2019 to 2024. As a full-time research scholar, balancing personal responsibilities and continuing her research without stable financial support was challenging.

She also experienced difficulty in accessing research materials and digital resources, attending conferences, conducting fieldwork, collecting data, travelling for academic purposes and undertaking publication-related activities. Limited financial support affected her ability to focus completely on her doctoral research.

Despite these constraints, Dr Janaki remained committed to her academic journey. She aspired to complete her Ph.D. and become a dedicated academician and researcher in the field of education, with a focus on teacher education, digital education and quality research in higher education institutions.

Dr Janaki comes from a modest family background where education was considered important despite financial limitations. Her family continuously encouraged her higher education journey, but meeting the expenses associated with full-time research placed considerable pressure on the household.

She began receiving assistance under the NFSC Scheme in September 2019. Under the Scheme, she received a Senior Research Fellowship of ₹35,000 per month.

The fellowship helped her manage expenses related to research materials, internet access, data collection, academic travel and publication activities. It reduced financial stress and enabled her to focus more effectively on completing her Ph.D. with confidence and dedication.

Beyond financial assistance, the NFSC fellowship provided Dr Janaki with stability and motivation throughout her doctoral journey. It supported her academic activities, research work and professional development while reducing the financial burden on her family.

With the support received under the NFSC Scheme, she gained the confidence to continue her Ph.D. research without interruption and devote greater attention to academic activities, research publications and professional development. The assistance strengthened both her professional growth and personal confidence.

Dr Janaki is currently working as a Guest Teacher at The Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University). The fellowship has strengthened her academic career path and enabled her to move closer to her goal of contributing to education through teaching and research.

Dr Janaki expressed her gratitude for the fellowship support and said,

“The NFSC fellowship provided me with financial stability and the confidence to continue my Ph.D. research without interruption. It reduced the financial burden on my family, supported my research and professional development, and strengthened my path towards a career in teaching and research.”

Through determination and support under the NFSC Scheme, Dr Janaki progressed from facing financial challenges during full-time research to completing her Ph.D. and pursuing an academic career. Her journey reflects the important role of fellowship assistance in advancing research aspirations and strengthening professional opportunities.

headline: Ex-Mill Sugar Prices Decline by Around 20%; Retail Prices Begin Downward Movement
fullText:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

Ex-Mill Sugar Prices Decline by Around 20%; Retail Prices Begin Downward Movement

Government Measures Improve Market Availability and Ensure Faster Movement of Sugar

28 AUG 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has taken a series of proactive measures to ensure adequate availability of sugar and prevent artificial tightening of supplies in the domestic market. Ex-mill sugar prices have declined by around 20% in recent days, while retail sugar prices have also started coming down. Given the normal transmission of changes through the supply chain, retail prices are expected to follow the downward movement in ex-mill prices shortly.

The Government has been closely monitoring sugar prices, stocks and movement across the country and has taken a series of proactive measures to ensure that the benefit of adequate availability reaches consumers. The downward trend in ex-mill and retail prices reflects that the sharp spike in prices witnessed recently was primarily on account of hoarding and speculation although the country carries adequate stocks of sugar.

Physical Verification Confirms Adequate Sugar Stocks

A nationwide drive for physical verification of sugar stocks at mills has reaffirmed the comfortable availability position. In several cases, sugar mills were found to be holding stocks higher than those declared in their monthly returns submitted to the Government. The verification exercise has established that there is no shortage of sugar in the country and there is no justification for panic buying or excessive stocking. In some cases, sugar mills were also found to be resorting to short selling, i.e. selling less sugar than the quantity allocated to them under the monthly quota. Such practices tend to unnecessarily constrain market supplies despite adequate physical stocks.

Fortnightly Sugar Quota System from September

The Government has also observed that, in certain cases, sugar sold by mills at the beginning of the month was being dispatched or lifted by buyers only towards the end of the month. This practice contributed to artificial scarcity in the market. To address such issues and ensure that sugar reaches the market in a timely manner, Government has decided to introduce a fortnightly sugar allocation system from September, replacing the existing monthly quota system. Under the fortnightly quota, mills will be required to sell at least 40% of the allocation in the first week and remaining quantity in the succeeding week.

The fortnightly system will enable the Government to:

Closely monitor demand and supply

Respond quickly to changes in market conditions

Prevent artificial tightening of supplies

Release additional quota whenever required to maintain adequate market availability.

This flexible mechanism will ensure that sugar supply remains aligned with actual domestic demand.

Sugar to be Dispatched within Seven Days of Sale

Sugar mills have already been directed to ensure that sugar sold is dispatched from the mill within seven days of sale. The combination of fortnightly quota allocation and mandatory dispatch within seven days will significantly improve the movement of sugar through the supply chain. It will ensure that sugar moves quickly from mills to dealers and ultimately to consumers, while discouraging unnecessary accumulation and speculative holding of stocks. Bulk consumers of sugar have also been advised not to accumulate stocks in excess of their operational requirements.

New Sugar Season to Further Strengthen Availability

Sugarcane crushing for the new season will commence from 15th October. It is expected that more than 10 LMT of sugar will be produced during the month. The Government has also permitted sugar mills to sell sugar produced during October without restriction, ensuring that new-season production becomes available in the domestic market at the earliest. Sugar production is expected to be around 45 LMT in November, providing substantial additional supplies for domestic consumption.

Government Assures Consumers of Adequate Sugar Availability

The Government once again assures consumers that there is no shortage of sugar in the country and that all necessary measures will be taken to ensure adequate and continuous availability of sugar at reasonable prices across the country, particularly during the forthcoming festive season.

Ex-mill sugar prices have declined by around 20% in recent days, and retail prices have also started declining from yesterday. Retail prices are expected to follow the downward trend in ex-mill prices shortly.

Government stock verification confirms adequate availability of sugar. In several cases, sugar mills were found to have stocks higher than those declared in their monthly returns.

Weekly sugar quota allocation from September will replace the monthly quota system, enabling the Government to monitor the market on a near real-time basis and release additional quota whenever required.

Sugar sold by mills must be dispatched within seven days, ensuring faster movement of sugar from mills to dealers and the domestic market and preventing unnecessary stock accumulation.

Additional sugar is entering the market: refiners have been permitted to sell converted sugar brought under the Advance Authorisation Scheme, while dealers/bulk consumers holding excess stocks are also offloading sugar.

Early crushing and new-season production will significantly strengthen availability: operational mills in Karnataka and Maharashtra are expected to add around 2 LMT during September, while more than 10 LMT is expected to be produced in October and around 45 LMT in November.

headline: Less procedural burden, wider global market access for Indian industry: Defence Export SOP and Open General Export Licence framework simplified to make India a trusted global manufacturing & export partner
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Less procedural burden, wider global market access for Indian industry: Defence Export SOP and Open General Export Licence framework simplified to make India a trusted global manufacturing & export partner

28 AUG 2026 1:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence has undertaken a comprehensive set of reforms to simplify the Defence Export Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and the Open General Export Licence (OGEL) framework, in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of making India a reliable, competitive and trusted global defence manufacturing and export partner, while advancing the objectives of Make-in-India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Undertaken under the guidance of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, these reforms seek to reduce procedural requirements, facilitate faster access to international markets and enable Indian defence companies to respond more effectively to global business opportunities, while ensuring that national security considerations remain fully safeguarded.

DEFENCE EXPORT SOP

Stakeholder consultation has been dispensed with for exports of non-lethal defence items to most destinations, while appropriate safeguards have been retained for sensitive countries.

Stakeholder consultation has been dispensed with for exports of all items for international tenders and exhibitions, enabling Indian companies to showcase their products and pursue international opportunities more expeditiously.

The OGEL is a standing one-time export authorisation that enables eligible exporters to self-generate export authorisations for multiple consignments of specified defence items, without seeking a separate authorisation for each consignment. It provides greater flexibility while reducing repetitive procedural requirements.

Three existing OGEL SOPs covering major platforms and equipment, parts and components, and intra-company transfer of technology have been consolidated into one unified OGEL SOP, providing exporters with a common and simpler framework.

OGEL validity has been increased from two to three years, reducing the frequency of renewals and associated compliance requirements.

OGEL coverage has been expanded from 41 to all countries, except negative/sensitive nations and those facing UN Security Council sanctions or arms embargoes.

A new provision facilitates Indian companies having long-term contracts or agreements with Foreign Original Equipment Manufacturers (FOEMs). OGEL may be granted for eligible items and the particular FOEM, with validity aligned with the underlying contract or agreement, subject to prescribed conditions.

The range of items covered under OGEL has been expanded, providing greater flexibility to eligible exporters. The revised framework also permits civil-end-use exports of specified parts and components of small-calibre arms and protective equipment, further broadening legitimate international business opportunities.

The reforms move India’s defence export regime towards a more comprehensive and facilitation-based system, reducing routine procedural requirements while retaining appropriate safeguards for sensitive items, technologies and destinations. The measures are expected to particularly benefit Indian defence manufacturers, including MSMEs, by enabling them to respond more quickly to international tenders and exhibitions, access wider global markets and reduce repetitive authorisation requirements. With defence production reaching an all-time high of Rs 1.78 lakh crore and defence exports touching a record figure of Rs 38,424 crore in FY 2025-26, these reforms further strengthen the momentum of India’s defence manufacturing and export ecosystem.

headline: Government Strengthens Monitoring and Timely Delivery of Scheduled Caste Welfare Schemes
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Monitoring and Timely Delivery of Scheduled Caste Welfare Schemes

Regular Reviews, Direct Benefit Transfer and Social Audits Support Effective Fund Utilisation

Coordinated Action with States and Union Territories Focuses on Timely Delivery to Beneficiaries

28 AUG 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Government is implementing a comprehensive range of welfare schemes for the educational advancement, socio-economic empowerment, livelihood promotion and protection of Scheduled Caste communities across the country.

During the financial years 2021-22 to 2025-26, funds were allocated for major initiatives including the Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students, National Fellowship for SC Students, National Overseas Scholarship, Top Class Education, Free Coaching, Pre-Matric Scholarship, Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), Scheme of Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA), Venture Capital Fund for SCs and skill-development programmes.

The implementation and utilisation of funds under various Scheduled Caste welfare schemes are undertaken in coordination with the respective States and Union Territories. Release of funds is linked to the receipt of complete proposals, submission of Utilisation Certificates, onboarding onto SNA-SPARSH wherever applicable, adherence to scheme guidelines and compliance with the prescribed financial norms.

To improve expenditure and strengthen accountability, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment conducts regular internal reviews of the schemes. Third-party evaluations and social audits are also undertaken to assess implementation and enhance the effectiveness of programme delivery.

Scholarship assistance is largely disbursed through the Direct Benefit Transfer mode to facilitate faster and more transparent transfer of benefits directly into the bank accounts of eligible students. This mechanism also supports accurate beneficiary targeting and reduces delays in disbursement.

The Ministry regularly monitors scheme implementation through national-level Chintan Shivirs, regional meetings, national conferences and consultations with stakeholders and officials from States and Union Territories.

Monthly and quarterly expenditure targets are reviewed to identify implementation gaps and facilitate timely corrective measures. Awareness and outreach initiatives are also undertaken through advertisements in national and regional newspapers, social media campaigns and regular follow-up with States and Union Territories.

These efforts are aimed at increasing awareness among eligible beneficiaries, improving the submission of proposals and ensuring timely utilisation of allocated funds.

Through strengthened monitoring, digital fund-management systems, direct transfer of benefits, regular evaluation and closer coordination with implementing authorities, the Government remains committed to ensuring that Scheduled Caste welfare schemes reach eligible beneficiaries effectively.

The initiatives seek to advance education, dignity, livelihood security and socio-economic empowerment among Scheduled Caste communities across the country.

CTTC Bhubaneswar Lights up Young Minds:Trains Over 8,000 Engineering Students Through Summer Internship Programme 2026

Empowering Future Engineers through Industry-graded Internship Training

28 AUG 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

In a shining testament to India's growing emphasis on industry-grade training, the Central Tool Room & Training Centre (CTTC), Bhubaneswar, under Ministry of MSME, has successfully conducted four-week Summer Internship Training Programme during May & June 2026, providing industry-oriented, hands-on training to 8,083 engineering students from 22 States and Union Territories across the country, including 26 international students from Sudan and Yemen.

The Training Programme provided an opportunity for engineering students from first year to final year and witnessed participation from across the country, including international students. The programme stands as a proud reaffirmation of CTTC Bhubaneswar's role as a premier institution for offering structured and industry-oriented training designed to sharpen the employability and technical competence of India's youth.

A Spectrum of Opportunity

Spanning disciplines as varied as Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, Civil, and Computer Science, the programme also focused on emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI - ML), Cloud Computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), and Additive Manufacturing. Each four-week course was designed to provide intensive hands-on training, bridging the gap between classroom learning and industrial practice.

Of the 8,083 students trained, the Mechanical discipline led the way with 3,193 candidates, followed by Electronics with 2,209; IT & Software with 1,948; Civil with 388, and other emerging domains accounting for 345- a spread that reflects both the enduring strength of core engineering and the rising pull of new-age technologies. The programme offered training across 39 engineering and emerging technology domains, with the highest participation in Artificial Intelligence (1,748 students), PLC Programming (1,000), AutoCAD (991), Python Programming (413) and Data Analytics (392).

The internship also attracted students from premier institutions such as the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), National Institutes of Technology (NITs), various Deemed-to-be Universities, engineering colleges, and polytechnic institutes.

About CTTC, Bhubaneswar-

Central Tool Room & Training Centre, Bhubaneswar has been set up to fulfill the tooling and training needs of the Micro, Small & Medium enterprises in the field of Tool Design and Manufacture and training of technical personnel in these fields.

The Centre Offers various services in the area of Auto parts, high precision parts, General Engineering sector by designing, development and manufacturing of quality press tools, moulds & dies, gauges, jigs & fixtures, etc. It also provides training/programmes in Tool & Die technology, Product Design, Mechatronics, Advance Machine Maintenance, CAD/CAM/CAE, CNC machining and programming, etc.

It has manufactured & supplied 437 types of 54,000 precision components to India Space Research Organization (ISRO) for Chandrayaan-3 Mission launched on 14th July, 2023.

It has also manufactured & supplied different types of precision components like regulator, flow control valves, gyroscope, temperature sensor & navigation parts to ISRO for Aditya – L1 Mission (Indian Solar Mission) launched on 02nd September, 2023.

The Centre has also made significant contributions to the aerospace and defence sectors by manufacturing high-precision components for Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), including components for the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) programme, thereby supporting indigenous manufacturing capabilities.
